n: An anointed messenger speaks: God’s Spirit is on him to bring good news to the humble, heal broken hearts, free captives, and open prison doors. In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus read this and declared, “This day is this scripture fulfilled.”

f.w: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me
the opening of the prison to them that are bound

n: He announces the year of the Lord’s favor—like the jubilee year when debts were forgiven and slaves freed—and the day of God’s vengeance, and comforts all who mourn. Notably, Jesus stopped reading before “the day of vengeance,” suggesting that part belongs to His Second Coming.

f.w: the acceptable year of the LORD
f.g: The year of God’s favor, recalling the jubilee (Leviticus 25:10).

f.w: the day of vengeance of our God

n: He gives mourners a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of grief, and a garment of praise instead of a heavy spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, planted by the Lord. In Hebrew “beauty” (pe’er) and “ashes” (efer) rhyme.

f.g: A headdress or garland instead of the ashes mourners put on their heads; a wordplay in Hebrew.
Fragrant oil used at festive occasions instead of mourning.

n: These healed people will rebuild ancient ruins and restore cities devastated for generations.

f.w: they shall build the old wastes

n: Foreigners will tend the flocks and fields, freeing Israel for a holy calling.
Israel will be called “Priests of the Lord” and “Ministers of our God”—fulfilling God’s original intent for them to be a kingdom of priests. Peter applies this to all believers.

f.w: ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD

n: Instead of shame, they receive a double portion—the firstborn’s inheritance—and everlasting joy.

f.g: A double portion was the firstborn son’s inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17).

n: The Lord loves justice and hates robbery even when disguised as offerings. He will faithfully reward His people and make an everlasting covenant with them.

f.w: I hate robbery for burnt offering
f.g: Possibly “robbery and wrongdoing”; God despises worship funded by injustice.

n: Their descendants will be recognized among the nations as a people blessed by the Lord.

f.w: the seed which the LORD hath blessed

n: A song of joy: God has dressed me in garments of salvation and a robe of righteousness, like a groom with a festive headdress or a bride wearing her jewels. Nephi prayed for the Lord to encircle him in “the robe of thy righteousness.”

f.w: as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments
f.g: The Hebrew suggests a priestly turban worn like a crown.

n: As surely as earth makes seeds sprout in a garden, God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all nations.

f.w: as the earth bringeth forth her bud
